newsitem.title: UK: Science takes giant leap for mushroom-lovers.
newsitem.headline: Science takes giant leap for mushroom-lovers.

text.p: Scientists said on Wednesday they had taken a giant leap forward for mushroom-lovers by growing the increasingly rare golden chanterelle in a greenhouse.
The delicacy had, until now, defied attempts at cultivation. It grew only in mature pine forests.

But Eric Danell of the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences in Uppsala and Francisco Camacho of Oregon State University said in the New Scientist magazine that hey had managed to grow golden chanterelles on pine seedlings in a laboratory.
Truffles, the most flavourful of the fungi, are already grown this way.
Some gourmets complain that cultivated mushrooms do not taste as good as the wild species. But chanterelles are on the decline in Europe and now have to be imported from the United States.

Danell and Camacho said they hoped they could turn their hand to even rarer and more expensive species such as the matsutake mushroom, valued by Japanese aficionados. Some of the mushrooms have been reported selling at hundreds of dollars apiece.
